sections.title: How it works — in short
body: The app shows a melody as short fragments on a keyboard: "press this, then these two together". You watch, play it on your own real piano and go on. No sheet music to read.
• At the top pick a lesson (the list) and a view: "Falling notes", "Cards" or "Sheet + keys".
• Pick a fragment (#1, #2… or ‹ ›) — learn one at a time.
• Hear or watch the fragment, play it on the piano, tap Next.
• When a fragment works, mark it "Got it" (✓). Progress is saved.
No connected piano is needed: a "did I play it right" check happens only if you press keys on the screen or on the computer keyboard.

sections.title: View: Falling notes
body: Notes fall onto the keys, Synthesia-style. A bar touches its key exactly when the note sounds.
• The big bottom button: Play / Pause / Resume; a short "Get ready…" before the start.
• ⏮ From the start, 🔁 Loop (the fragment repeats), 🔊/🔇 sound.
• Speed 25–100 %. Start slow.
• Hands: Both, Left, Right — practise one hand, the other stays silent. Green is right, blue is left.
• 👁 Ahead: how many seconds of notes you see in advance (2 / 3 / 5).
• Tap a falling bar: playback pauses, the note sounds and a small menu opens — 🔊 Hear it, ⚑ Sounds wrong (see below), ✎ Fix it myself (coming later).
• At the top: the fragments and "Whole lesson"; next to them ✓ Got it.

• Notes on a fragment: tap Note (next to Got it) for the current fragment, or hold any fragment number for half a second (right-click on a Mac). Write a note, mark "Come back later", or tick a wish for re-cutting — Too hard — split it, Merge with the next, Boundary is wrong — and tap Save. The number then shows a pencil (a note) and a bookmark (come back later).

sections.title: "Wait for me" — and moving on without a keyboard
body: In ⏸ Wait for me the notes stop on the line by the keys, and the bar says what to play ("Play E4 + G4"). You go on when ready — three equal ways:
• Tap the big "Next ›" button at the bottom — the main way on an iPad.
• Press the right keys on the on-screen keyboard (all of a chord). The step moves on by itself; a wrong key flashes.
• Space on an attached keyboard does the same as Next.
🔊 "Hear it" next to it plays the current step.

sections.title: View: Cards
body: Step by step: one card, one action ("Press E4", "Press together C4 + E4").
• Next › / ‹ Back, or swipe the card strip; tap a card to jump there and hear it.
• ▶ Step to hear a step, ▶ Fragment for the whole fragment, ⟳ loop, speed.
• ♩ Play along: silent, with a metronome and a one-bar count-in — play to the click.
• Keyboard colours: hand colour = press now, stripes = keep holding, ring = next step.
• Pressing the right keys on screen also moves to the next step.
• At the end of a fragment: Again, "Got it → next fragment" or just "Next fragment ›".

sections.title: View: Sheet + keys
body: Notation in sync with the keyboard — for getting used to notes bit by bit. Reading them is optional.
• ♪ Listen: ▶ / ■, ⟲ loop. ⇥ Steps: ‹ Back / Next › one note or chord at a time.
• Tap a note on the staff to hear it and see its key.
• Press a key to see where it sits on the staff (this does not move the step).
• "Names" (labels under notes) and "Hands" (hand colours) toggles, speed, ✓ Got it.

sections.title: Keyboard and on-screen keys
body: • The on-screen keyboard plays chords with several fingers and glissando — slide your finger.
• Space = the big button (play/pause or Next). ← / → switch fragments (in Cards and Steps: back / next).
• The computer keyboard as a piano: A W S E D F T G Y H U J K = C4 up to C5 (then O L P ;). Z / X — octave down / up.
The "Space = Next" hint shows only with a mouse or trackpad; Space works without it too.

sections.title: Sound on an iPad
body: The browser allows sound only after a touch, so your first tap on the page turns it on. If you see "Tap to enable sound", tap.
The app plays even with the iPad in silent mode. If it is quiet: check the volume, the 🔊 button in the view and that the tab is not muted; then reload and tap the screen.
Until the grand-piano samples load from the internet, the first notes sound with a simple synth.

sections.title: Where lessons come from
body: • An agent (Claude Code) makes a lesson from a YouTube video, audio or MIDI: tell it "make a lesson from this video <link>" — it transcribes the notes and uploads the lesson through the API.
• ⤒ Import — a .mid / .midi, .musicxml / .xml / .mxl or lesson .json file. The lesson appears in the list and opens.
• 🎧 Original — when a lesson came from YouTube, opens the video right at the current fragment. Handy to compare by ear.
Lessons live in the database on your computer, not on the internet.

sections.title: "Sounds wrong" — what it does
body: Transcribing notes from a video is not perfect. There are two ways to report what sounds wrong:

• One note: tap its falling bar (Falling notes view). In the menu pick what is wrong — Should be higher, Should be lower, Extra note, A note is missing, Wrong timing, Other — add a comment if you like, and tap Save report. The report remembers that exact note.
• A whole fragment: tap ⚑ Sounds wrong at the top right and describe it in words ("the second bar should be a different, lower note").
What happens next, honestly:
• The app only stores the report in a queue. It does not fix the lesson by itself.

• An agent fixes it: tell Claude Code "check the feedback queue" (the /transcribe skill). It goes to the reported note or fragment, re-transcribes it from the original or corrects it with you listening, and marks the report fixed — or says why it could not.
• Without an agent: fix it by hand — open the original (🎧), find the right notes and import a corrected lesson.
Your reports and what became of them (open, in progress, fixed, won't fix, with the agent's note) are listed under the form in ⚑ Sounds wrong.

The same window has a second tab, Notes on fragments: every note of the lesson, with "Only Come back later" to filter and Done to remove one. Tell Claude Code "look at my notes on this lesson" to go through them together.
The more specific (which note, higher or lower, which hand), the better the fix.

sections.title: Settings (⚙)
body: • Note names: C D E or Do Re Mi. Labels on keys: all / C only / none.
• Language UA / EN, theme (Auto → Light → Dark).
• API token — only if the server asks for one: without it imports, reports and progress are not saved.
The chosen lesson and view are remembered, and the address-bar link opens exactly them. If the server is unreachable, demo lessons are shown.
